policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 5:1 reads 'the country of the Gerasenes', transliterating Γερασηνῶν rather than Γαδαρηνῶν ('Gadarenes').
Genitive absolute vs. dative participle is a Greek construction difference; ASV 'And when he was come out of the boat' renders either identically.
εὐθύς/εὐθέως are orthographic variants both rendered 'straightway', and ὑπήντησεν/ἀπήντησεν both 'there met him'; the English distinguishes neither.
ASV 5:3 'could any more bind him, no, not with a chain' renders οὐκέτι ('any more'), which the RP reading lacks, and the singular ἁλύσει rather than plural ἁλύσεσιν.
Pure transposition of ἴσχυεν and αὐτόν; ASV 'no man had strength to tame him' cannot show Greek word order.
ASV 5:5 'in the tombs and in the mountains' follows the base order μνήμασιν … ὄρεσιν, not the RP transposition 'in the mountains and in the tombs'.
Connective καί vs. postpositive δέ with the same participle; ASV's sentence-initial 'And when he saw' renders either conjunction.
Accusative vs. dative object of προσεκύνησεν; ASV 'worshipped him' renders both, and the attached note concerns the sense of the Greek verb, not the case.
ASV 5:7 'he saith' is a present, rendering λέγει; the aorist εἶπεν would be 'he said'.
Transposition of ὄνομά and σοι; ASV 'What is thy name?' cannot show it.
ASV 5:9 'And he saith unto him' renders λέγει αὐτῷ; the RP reading ἀπεκρίθη λέγων would give 'he answered, saying', which the ASV does not have.
Λεγιών/Λεγεών is a spelling variant of the same name; ASV 'Legion' renders either.
Neuter αὐτά vs. masculine αὐτούς; English 'them' carries no gender.
ASV 5:12 'And they besought him, saying' has no rendering of the RP addition πάντες οἱ δαίμονες ('all the demons'), which the ASV would have had to translate.
ASV 5:13 'And he gave them leave' lacks any rendering of the RP addition εὐθέως ὁ Ἰησοῦς ('straightway Jesus'), and keeps the pronoun subject.
ASV 5:13 gives the number as an appositional phrase, 'in number about two thousand', not as the separate finite clause ἦσαν δέ ('and they were about two thousand').
Connective καί vs. postpositive δέ; ASV's 'And they that fed them fled' renders either.
ASV 5:14 'they that fed them' renders the pronoun αὐτούς; the RP reading τοὺς χοίρους would give 'they that fed the swine'.
ἀπήγγειλαν and ἀνήγγειλαν differ only in prefix and are both rendered 'told it'.
ASV 5:14 'And they came to see' renders the simple ἦλθον; the compound ἐξῆλθον would be 'went out' / 'came forth'.
ASV 5:15 'sitting, clothed and in his right mind' has no conjunction between 'sitting' and 'clothed', so it does not render the RP καί added after καθήμενον.
λεγιῶνα/Λεγεῶνα is a spelling variant; ASV 'the legion' renders either.
Connective καί vs. postpositive δέ; ASV 'And they that saw it declared' renders either.
ASV 5:18 'And as he was entering into the boat' renders the present participle ἐμβαίνοντος; the aorist ἐμβάντος would be 'when he had entered'.
Transposition of μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ and ᾖ; ASV 'that he might be with him' cannot show it.
ASV 5:19 'And he suffered him not' keeps a pronoun subject and does not render the RP explicit subject ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
ἀπάγγειλον and ἀνάγγειλον differ only in prefix and are both rendered 'tell them'.
Transposition of ὁ κύριος and σοι; ASV 'how great things the Lord hath done for thee' cannot show Greek order.
ASV 5:22 'And there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue' has no 'behold', so it does not render the RP addition ἰδού.
ASV 5:23 'and beseecheth him much' is a present, matching παρακαλεῖ and the historic present 'there cometh' of v. 22; the imperfect παρεκάλει would be 'was beseeching'.
Transposition of τὰς χεῖρας and αὐτῇ; ASV 'lay thy hands on her' cannot show it.
ἵνα and ὅπως are both rendered by the purpose 'that she may be made whole'.
Aorist subjunctive ζήσῃ vs. future ζήσεται, both inside the same 'that … and live' clause; the ASV wording distinguishes neither.
ASV 5:25 reads 'And a woman'; the ASV renders the indefinite τις as 'a certain', so the RP addition is not represented.
Transposition of δώδεκα and ἔτη; ASV 'twelve years' cannot show Greek order.
ASV 5:27 'having heard the things concerning Jesus' renders an articular τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ with 'the things' set in roman, not as an italicized supply.
The candidates differ by transposition and by the bracketing of τῶν ἱματίων; ASV 'If I touch but his garments' renders the same words in English order and settles neither.
εὐθύς/εὐθέως is an orthographic variant; ASV 'And straightway' renders either.
εὐθύς/εὐθέως is an orthographic variant; ASV 'And straightway Jesus' renders either.
Bare dative vs. ἐπί with the dative after γέγονεν; ASV 'what had been done to her' renders either.
Nominative-for-vocative Θυγάτηρ vs. vocative θύγατερ; English 'Daughter' as address is the same for both.
ASV 5:36 'not heeding the word spoken', with the margin 'Or, overhearing', renders παρακούσας; the RP εὐθέως ἀκούσας would give 'straightway hearing' and no such margin.
ASV 'to follow with him' can render μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ or the dative αὐτῷ governed by the συν- prefix of συνακολουθῆσαι.
Presence or absence of the Greek article before ἀδελφόν; English 'the brother of James' requires its own article either way.
ASV 5:38 'And they come to the house' renders the plural ἔρχονται; the singular ἔρχεται would be 'he cometh'.
ASV 5:38 'and he beholdeth a tumult' has the connective 'and', which the RP asyndeton omits.
Emphatic αὐτὸς δέ vs. articular ὁ δέ as subject; ASV 'But he, having put them all forth' renders both as a plain pronoun.
ASV 5:40 'where the child was' has no participle 'lying', so it does not render the RP addition ἀνακείμενον.
ASV 5:41 transliterates 'Talitha cumi' with a final vowel, matching κοῦμι; κουμ would give 'cum'.
ἔγειρε vs. ἔγειραι are alternative imperative forms of the same verb, both rendered 'Arise'.
εὐθύς/εὐθέως is an orthographic variant; ASV 'And straightway the damsel rose up' renders either.
ASV 5:42 'And they were amazed straightway with a great amazement' renders the second εὐθύς, which the RP reading omits.
